chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Catholic today, with his wife and five children
summary: He is a Catholic, as are his wife, daughter and son; he has four girls and a boy, ages 14 to 34.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: So are we. Fancy that. Isn't that nice?
Oh, that's really nice. That's lovely. Is your wife a Catholic, too?
How nice. And your daughter, too?
I have a lot of kids.
Well, how many kids have you got?
Well, I have four girls and a boy.
Fancy that. Where do they all fit in?
That's my baby, yeah. ^That's Michelle. Just came in.
Little Michelle. And what about your other children?
Well, Gus, he's at work right now.
No, that's right, he's in the room back there. He's asleep. I thought he was at work.
Oh, we better not make too much row.
Gus is 18, and Marcia Ann, you didn't see her, she is 16. And I have Patsy, she's 20, and my oldest girl, I think she's 34.
Oh, I see, you have a gap there.
Oh, yes, I didn't think there was going to be any more after my first one.
I always wanted alls a boy, see. But it didn't come up that way. It came out the other way.

Fancy that. Well, I can't believe that Michelle. I said to my daughter, 'How old do you think Mr. Johnson's daughter was?' Well, she said, 'Gosh, I really couldn't tell you.' We thought she was probably 18 or 20 or something.
No. Oh, she thinks she is, you know.
Oh, yes, that's right. Well, it transfers on the phone.
